subject.title: [Feature]: Add before_persistence_write hook for durable state changes

question: Should OpenClaw add a dedicated `before_persistence_write` hook for durable state changes, or represent durable-write policy through existing/enriched tool and provenance hooks instead?
rationale: This defines a public Plugin SDK security boundary over persisted user and agent state, including what data plugins can see, whether they can block or mutate writes, and how plugin failures affect durable state.

options.title: Design a dedicated durable-write hook
options.body: Add a narrow `before_persistence_write` contract with redacted targets, block/mutation rules, failure policy, docs, and representative writer coverage after maintainer/security review.

options.title: Fold durable context into existing hooks
options.body: Extend `before_tool_call` and related provenance/read-time APIs instead of adding a new hook family, reducing hook count but requiring broader taxonomy work first.

options.title: Defer to the provenance model
options.body: Keep this issue as a dependency of the persistent-state provenance design until maintainers settle the end-to-end trust model.

recommendation.title: Design a dedicated durable-write hook
recommendation.body: Add a narrow `before_persistence_write` contract with redacted targets, block/mutation rules, failure policy, docs, and representative writer coverage after maintainer/security review.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc has the strongest hook-contract and adjacent operator-policy history among the inspected owners.
